Mark 1: Jesus called fishermen in the middle of their workday. What would it have cost them to leave, and what would it cost us?
Mark 2: The friends broke through a roof for someone they loved. Who could we carry to Jesus together?
Mark 3: Jesus' own family thought he was out of his mind. How do we handle it when people close to us misunderstand our faith?
Mark 4: Which kind of soil best describes each of us this season, and why?
Mark 5: The healed man wanted to follow Jesus, but Jesus sent him home to tell his family. Where is our 'home' mission field?
Mark 6: Jesus' hometown couldn't see past 'the carpenter'. Do we ever limit each other by who we used to be?
Mark 7: The Syrophoenician woman would not give up. Is there something we've stopped praying for that we should pick up again together?
Mark 8: If Jesus asked each of us 'Who do you say I am?', what would we answer today?
Mark 9: 'I believe; help my unbelief.' Where do we each need that prayer right now?
Mark 10: The rich young man walked away sad. What would be hardest for us to let go of?
Mark 11: Jesus cleared space for prayer in the temple. What crowds out prayer in our home?
Mark 12: The widow gave everything she had. What does generosity look like for us as a couple?
Mark 13: Jesus says to stay awake and watchful. What helps us stay spiritually alert in a busy life?
Mark 14: The disciples fell asleep while Jesus prayed. When have we let each other down, and how did grace show up?
Mark 15: Simon of Cyrene was pulled out of the crowd to carry the cross. How might we help carry someone's burden this week?
Mark 16: The women ran from the tomb afraid. What do we find hardest to believe or share about the resurrection?
James 1: James says to be quick to listen and slow to speak. How are we doing with that in our own conversations?
James 2: Do we treat some people better because of how they look or what they have? Where might that show up for us?
James 3: Words can start fires. Is there something one of us said this week that needs mending?
James 4: 'If the Lord wills.' How do we hold our plans for the future together?
James 5: James tells us to pray for one another. What can we each pray for the other this week?
Luke 1: Mary said yes to something that would turn her life upside down. What has God asked of us that took courage?
Luke 2: Mary 'treasured up all these things'. What moments from our life together do we want to treasure?
Luke 3: John told people to share and be honest in their work. What would 'fruit of repentance' look like in our daily routine?
Luke 4: Jesus answered each temptation with Scripture. Is there a verse we could both memorize this month?
Luke 5: Peter said, 'Depart from me, I am a sinful man,' but Jesus called him anyway. How does that encourage us?
Luke 6: Which of the Beatitudes speaks to each of us most right now?
Luke 7: The woman who was forgiven much loved much. How has being forgiven changed us?
Luke 8: Jesus slept through the storm. What storm are we in, and how can we trust him in it together?
Luke 9: Jesus sent the twelve out with very little. What do we hold onto 'just in case'?
Luke 10: Are we more like Martha or Mary? How can we make room for both in our home?
Luke 11: The disciples asked, 'Teach us to pray.' What would help us pray together more often?
Luke 12: Jesus says not to worry. What is each of us worried about that we could hand over together?
Luke 13: The fig tree got one more year of care. Who in our lives needs that kind of patience from us?
Luke 14: Who could we invite to our table who can't repay us?
Luke 15: Which son do we identify with more, the younger or the older, and why?
Luke 16: Jesus says faithfulness in little things matters. What 'little things' could we be more faithful in?
Luke 17: Only one of ten came back to say thank you. What are we grateful for today?
Luke 18: The widow kept asking. Is there something we should keep praying for together?
Luke 19: Zacchaeus changed his whole life after one meal with Jesus. What would it look like for our home to be that kind of place?
Luke 20: 'Give to God what is God's.' What belongs to God in our life that we've been holding back?
Luke 21: The widow gave out of her poverty. How do we decide what to give?
Luke 22: Jesus served at the table and then washed feet. How can we serve each other in small ways this week?
Luke 23: The thief on the cross was welcomed at the last moment. What does that say about God's grace?
Luke 24: The disciples' hearts burned as Jesus opened the Scriptures. When has the Bible come alive for us?
Acts 1: The disciples waited and prayed together before anything happened. How do we wait well together?
Acts 2: The first believers shared meals, prayer and possessions. Which of those could we grow in?
Acts 3: Peter said, 'What I have I give you.' What do we have to give, even if it isn't money?
Acts 4: Peter and John spoke boldly. What helps us speak about our faith with courage?
Acts 5: Ananias and Sapphira agreed together to deceive. How do we keep each other honest?
Acts 6: The church chose people to care for widows so no one was overlooked. Who might be overlooked around us?
Acts 7: Stephen forgave those who killed him. Is there anyone we struggle to forgive?
Acts 8: Philip followed an unexpected prompting onto a desert road. Have we ever felt nudged to help someone unexpectedly?
Acts 9: Ananias was afraid to visit Saul but went anyway. Who might God be asking us to reach out to?
Acts 10: Peter had to unlearn his assumptions about who belonged. What assumptions might we need to unlearn?
Acts 11: Barnabas was known as an encourager. How can we encourage each other more?
Acts 12: The church prayed for Peter, then was surprised when he showed up. Do we expect our prayers to be answered?
Acts 13: The church sent Paul and Barnabas out with prayer. Who could we support in their calling?
Acts 14: Paul was stoned and then went back into the city. What keeps us going after a setback?
Acts 15: The council found a way for Jewish and Gentile believers to share meals. How do we handle disagreements with other believers?
Acts 16: Paul and Silas sang in prison at midnight. How do we respond to hard times together?
Acts 17: The Bereans checked everything against the Scriptures. How do we test what we hear?
Acts 18: Priscilla and Aquila worked, hosted and taught together as a couple. What could we learn from them?
Acts 19: The Ephesians burned their magic books, worth a fortune. Is there anything we should let go of?
Acts 20: Paul's farewell was full of tears and love. How do we want people to remember our marriage?
Acts 21: Paul's friends begged him not to go to Jerusalem, but he went. How do we decide when to go against well-meant advice?
Acts 22: Paul told his own story of meeting Jesus. How would each of us tell our own faith story?
Acts 23: Paul's nephew warned of a plot and saved his life. How has God used family to protect us?
Acts 24: Felix kept putting off his decision. Is there anything we keep putting off?
Acts 25: Festus didn't know what to make of Paul's case. How do we explain faith to people who find it puzzling?
Acts 26: Agrippa said, 'In a short time would you persuade me to be a Christian?' How do we share our faith without pressuring people?
Acts 27: In the middle of the storm, Paul urged everyone to eat and take courage. How can we be a steady presence for each other?
Acts 28: The islanders on Malta showed 'unusual kindness'. When has a stranger been kind to us?
Galatians 1: Paul says he wasn't trying to please people. Where do we feel pressure to please others?
Galatians 2: Paul confronted Peter to his face. How do we speak up when something is wrong between friends?
Galatians 3: 'You are all one in Christ Jesus.' What divisions does this cut across for us?
Galatians 4: We are called children and heirs, not slaves. How does that change how we see ourselves?
Galatians 5: Which fruit of the Spirit do we see in each other? Which would we like to grow?
Galatians 6: 'Bear one another's burdens.' What burden can each of us help the other carry this week?
1 Thessalonians 1: The Thessalonians' faith was talked about everywhere. What would we like our faith to be known for?
1 Thessalonians 2: Paul cared for them 'like a nursing mother'. Who has cared for our faith like that?
1 Thessalonians 3: Paul couldn't stop worrying until he heard they were okay. Who could we check on this week?
1 Thessalonians 4: Paul says to aspire to live quietly and work with our hands. What would a quieter life look like for us?
1 Thessalonians 5: 'Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances.' Which of these is hardest for each of us?
2 Thessalonians 1: Paul thanks God that their love for one another is growing. Where have we seen our love grow?
2 Thessalonians 2: Some were unsettled by rumours about the end times. How do we stay steady when things feel uncertain?
2 Thessalonians 3: 'Do not grow weary in doing good.' Where are we feeling weary right now?
1 Corinthians 1: The Corinthians were divided into camps. What causes division in churches today, and how can we avoid it?
1 Corinthians 2: Paul came in weakness, not with impressive speech. When has God used our weakness?
1 Corinthians 3: One plants, another waters, but God gives the growth. Who planted and watered faith in each of us?
1 Corinthians 4: Paul says it matters little how others judge him. How much do others' opinions shape us?
1 Corinthians 5: A little leaven spreads through the whole lump. What small habits shape our home?
1 Corinthians 6: 'You are not your own; you were bought with a price.' What does that mean for how we treat our bodies and time?
1 Corinthians 7: Paul gives practical advice about marriage. What has helped our marriage most?
1 Corinthians 8: Paul gave up his rights for the sake of others' consciences. Is there a freedom we could set aside out of love?
1 Corinthians 9: Paul compares faith to training for a race. What spiritual 'training' could we do together?
1 Corinthians 10: 'God is faithful, and he will not let you be tempted beyond your ability.' When have we seen that 'way of escape'?
1 Corinthians 11: The Lord's Supper is about remembering. What helps us remember Jesus in everyday life?
1 Corinthians 12: What gifts do we see in each other that the other might not recognize?
1 Corinthians 13: Read the love passage aloud, replacing 'love' with each other's name. Which line stands out?
1 Corinthians 14: Paul says everything should be done to build each other up. What builds us up most?
1 Corinthians 15: Paul says if Christ is not raised, our faith is in vain. How does the resurrection shape our hope?
1 Corinthians 16: 'Let all that you do be done in love.' What would change if we really lived that?
2 Corinthians 1: God comforts us so we can comfort others. When has our own hardship helped us comfort someone?
2 Corinthians 2: Paul urged the church to forgive and comfort someone who had repented. How quickly do we let things go?
2 Corinthians 3: 'Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.' Where do we each need freedom?
2 Corinthians 4: 'We have this treasure in jars of clay.' How do we feel about our own weaknesses?
2 Corinthians 5: Paul calls us ambassadors. Where are we 'posted', and who do we represent Christ to?
2 Corinthians 6: Paul lists everything he endured. What hardships have strengthened our faith?
2 Corinthians 7: Paul says godly grief leads to repentance without regret. How do we handle saying sorry to each other?
2 Corinthians 8: The poorer Macedonians gave generously. What would it look like to grow in generosity together?
2 Corinthians 9: 'God loves a cheerful giver.' Do we give cheerfully, or out of obligation?
2 Corinthians 10: Paul says to take every thought captive. Which thoughts do we each need to take captive?
2 Corinthians 11: Paul boasts about his weaknesses rather than his successes. What would we 'boast' about?
2 Corinthians 12: 'My grace is sufficient for you.' Where do we each need to hear that this week?
2 Corinthians 13: Paul says to examine yourselves. What would we each say about where we are in our faith?
Romans 1: Paul was 'not ashamed of the gospel'. When do we feel shy about our faith?
Romans 2: Paul warns against judging others while doing the same things. Where might we be guilty of that?
Romans 3: 'All have sinned and fall short.' How does knowing that change the way we treat each other?
Romans 4: Abraham 'hoped against hope'. What are we hoping for that seems unlikely?
Romans 5: Suffering produces endurance, character and hope. Where have we seen that in our lives?
Romans 6: Paul talks about walking in newness of life. What 'old' patterns are we leaving behind?
Romans 7: Paul says, 'I do not do what I want.' Where do we each feel that struggle?
Romans 8: 'Nothing can separate us from the love of God.' What does that promise mean to each of us?
Romans 9: Paul grieved for his own people who didn't believe. Who do we grieve for and pray for?
Romans 10: 'How beautiful are the feet of those who preach good news.' Who brought good news to us?
Romans 11: Paul ends his argument in praise of God's wisdom. What about God amazes us?
Romans 12: Which instruction in this chapter would make the biggest difference in our home?
Romans 13: 'Love does no wrong to a neighbour.' Who are our neighbours, literally and otherwise?
Romans 14: Paul asks believers not to judge each other over food and days. What do Christians argue about today that might fit here?
Romans 15: 'Welcome one another as Christ has welcomed you.' Who could we welcome more warmly?
Romans 16: Paul greets dozens of people by name, many of them women and couples. Who would we want to thank by name?
John 1: Andrew's first move was to bring his brother to Jesus. Who could we bring?
John 2: Mary told the servants, 'Do whatever he tells you.' What is Jesus telling us right now?
John 3: Nicodemus came at night with honest questions. What questions about faith do we still have?
John 4: Jesus crossed social lines to talk with the Samaritan woman. Who do we tend to avoid?
John 5: Jesus asked, 'Do you want to be healed?' Is there something we've grown used to that we should bring to him?
John 6: A boy's small lunch fed thousands. What small thing could we offer God?
John 7: 'If anyone thirsts, let him come to me.' What are we each thirsty for?
John 8: Jesus said to the accusers, 'Let him who is without sin cast the first stone.' When are we quick to judge?
John 9: The healed man said, 'I was blind, now I see.' What has faith helped us see differently?
John 10: Jesus says his sheep know his voice. How do we recognize God's voice?
John 11: Jesus wept with Mary and Martha even knowing he would raise Lazarus. How do we comfort each other in grief?
John 12: Mary poured out costly perfume. What is our most precious gift to God?
John 13: Jesus washed his disciples' feet. What is the 'foot washing' we can do for each other?
John 14: 'Let not your hearts be troubled.' What is troubling each of us right now?
John 15: 'Abide in me.' What helps us stay connected to Jesus day by day?
John 16: Jesus said, 'In the world you will have trouble, but take heart.' Where do we need to take heart?
John 17: Jesus prayed for unity among his followers. How do we stay united as a couple?
John 18: Peter denied Jesus three times by a fire. When have we been afraid to be known as his?
John 19: From the cross Jesus made sure his mother was cared for. How do we care for our parents and family?
John 20: Thomas needed to see for himself. Is it okay to have doubts? How do we talk about them?
John 21: Jesus asked Peter three times, 'Do you love me?' How would we each answer him today?
Ephesians 1: Paul prays that their eyes would be opened to their hope. What is our hope as a family?
Ephesians 2: 'By grace you have been saved.' How does grace show up in our marriage?
Ephesians 3: Paul prays they would grasp how wide and long and high and deep Christ's love is. How have we experienced that love?
Ephesians 4: 'Do not let the sun go down on your anger.' How are we doing with that?
Ephesians 5: Paul compares marriage to Christ and the church. What part of that picture speaks to us?
Ephesians 6: Which piece of the armour of God do we each need most right now?
Philippians 1: Paul found joy even in prison. Where do we find joy in hard circumstances?
Philippians 2: 'Count others more significant than yourselves.' How can we put each other first this week?
Philippians 3: Paul says, 'Forgetting what lies behind, I press on.' What do we need to leave behind?
Philippians 4: 'Whatever is true, honourable, just, pure, lovely...' What good things could we think on together?
Colossians 1: Paul says all things hold together in Christ. What does it look like for Christ to hold our life together?
Colossians 2: Paul warns against empty philosophies. What ideas around us pull us away from Christ?
Colossians 3: 'Put on compassion, kindness, humility, meekness and patience.' Which of these do we need more of at home?
Colossians 4: 'Let your speech always be gracious.' How do we talk to each other on our worst days?
Philemon 1: Paul asked Philemon to welcome back the man who had wronged him. Is there a relationship we need to restore?
Matthew 1: Joseph chose to protect Mary even before the angel spoke. What does that say about his character?
Matthew 2: The magi travelled far to worship. What would we be willing to go out of our way for?
Matthew 3: God said, 'This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.' Do we believe God delights in us?
Matthew 4: Jesus started his ministry by calling people to follow him. What does following Jesus look like in our daily routine?
Matthew 5: Jesus says to be salt and light. How can our home shine in our neighbourhood?
Matthew 6: Jesus says where our treasure is, our heart will be. Where is our treasure?
Matthew 7: The wise man built on rock. What are we building our family on?
Matthew 8: The centurion believed Jesus could heal from a distance. What would it look like to have faith like that?
Matthew 9: Jesus had compassion on the crowds, who were like sheep without a shepherd. Who are we moved to help?
Matthew 10: Jesus says even the hairs on our head are numbered. How does that make us feel?
Matthew 11: 'Come to me, all who are weary.' Where are we weary, and how can we rest in him?
Matthew 12: Jesus says good fruit comes from a good heart. What do our words say about our hearts?
Matthew 13: The man sold everything for the treasure in the field. What is worth everything to us?
Matthew 14: Peter walked on water until he looked at the waves. What are the 'waves' that distract us?
Matthew 15: Jesus says what comes out of the mouth reveals the heart. What came out of our mouths this week?
Matthew 16: Jesus said to take up our cross. What does that mean for us in practical terms?
Matthew 17: Faith like a mustard seed can move mountains. What 'mountain' are we facing?
Matthew 18: Jesus says to forgive seventy times seven. Is there something we keep needing to forgive?
Matthew 19: 'What God has joined together, let no one separate.' What protects our marriage?
Matthew 20: The workers hired last got the same wage. Does God's generosity ever bother us?
Matthew 21: The crowds praised Jesus one day and turned on him days later. How do we stay faithful when it's unpopular?
Matthew 22: Love God and love your neighbour. Which of these do we find harder?
Matthew 23: Jesus warned against doing good things to be seen. Do we ever do that?
Matthew 24: Jesus told his followers to be ready. What does being ready look like for us?
Matthew 25: 'As you did it to one of the least of these, you did it to me.' Who are 'the least of these' near us?
Matthew 26: The disciples couldn't stay awake one hour. How can we help each other stay faithful in prayer?
Matthew 27: Pilate washed his hands of responsibility. When are we tempted to look the other way?
Matthew 28: Jesus promised, 'I am with you always.' When have we felt his presence most?
1 Timothy 1: Paul calls himself the foremost of sinners. Why is it freeing to admit our weaknesses?
1 Timothy 2: Paul urges prayers for everyone, including leaders. Who could we pray for regularly?
1 Timothy 3: Leaders should manage their households well. What does a well-run home look like to us?
1 Timothy 4: 'Let no one despise you for your youth.' Who can we encourage who is young in faith?
1 Timothy 5: Paul says to care for widows and family members. Who in our family might need care?
1 Timothy 6: 'Godliness with contentment is great gain.' Are we content with what we have?
2 Timothy 1: Timothy's faith came through his grandmother and mother. What faith do we want to pass on?
2 Timothy 2: Paul compares faithfulness to a soldier, an athlete and a farmer. Which picture fits us best?
2 Timothy 3: Paul says all Scripture is useful. How has reading the Bible together been for us so far?
2 Timothy 4: 'I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race.' What do we want to be able to say at the end?
Titus 1: Paul tells Titus to put things in order. What needs putting in order in our life?
Titus 2: Older believers are to teach and encourage younger ones. Who mentors us, and who could we mentor?
Titus 3: Paul reminds us we were once foolish too. How does that make us more patient with others?
Hebrews 1: Hebrews opens with how God spoke through his Son. What has Jesus shown us about God?
Hebrews 2: Jesus was made like us in every way. Does it help to know he understands our struggles?
Hebrews 3: 'Encourage one another daily.' How can we do this more?
Hebrews 4: We can approach God's throne with confidence. What would we like to bring to him?
Hebrews 5: The writer says some needed milk, not solid food. How are we growing in faith?
Hebrews 6: Hope is described as an anchor for the soul. What anchors us when life is stormy?
Hebrews 7: Jesus 'always lives to intercede' for us. What does it mean that Jesus is praying for us?
Hebrews 8: God promises to write his law on our hearts. How has God changed our hearts over time?
Hebrews 9: The old sacrifices pointed to Christ. What does Jesus' sacrifice mean to each of us?
Hebrews 10: 'Do not neglect to meet together.' How important is church community to us?
Hebrews 11: Which hero of faith in this chapter do we relate to most?
Hebrews 12: 'Run with endurance the race set before us.' What helps us keep going?
Hebrews 13: 'Show hospitality to strangers.' How can we open our home more?
1 Peter 1: Peter calls his readers exiles. Do we ever feel like strangers in our culture?
1 Peter 2: Peter says to live such good lives that others notice. What do our neighbours see in us?
1 Peter 3: Peter says to always be ready to give a reason for our hope. How would we each explain our hope?
1 Peter 4: 'Love covers a multitude of sins.' How has love covered faults in our marriage?
1 Peter 5: 'Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.' What anxieties can we hand over today?
2 Peter 1: Peter lists faith, virtue, knowledge, self-control, steadfastness, godliness, kindness and love. Which are we growing in?
2 Peter 2: Peter warns of false teachers. How do we recognize teaching that leads us astray?
2 Peter 3: God is patient, not wanting anyone to perish. How can we be patient with people who don't believe yet?
Jude 1: Jude says to keep ourselves in God's love. What practices help us do that?
1 John 1: 'If we confess our sins, he is faithful to forgive.' Is confession part of our life together?
1 John 2: John says whoever claims to be in the light but hates a brother is still in darkness. Is there anyone we hold resentment against?
1 John 3: 'Let us love not in word but in deed.' What loving deed could we do together this week?
1 John 4: 'Perfect love casts out fear.' What fears do we each need God's love to overcome?
1 John 5: John wrote so we may know we have eternal life. How confident are we in that?
2 John 1: John says to walk in love. What does walking in love look like in everyday life?
3 John 1: Gaius was praised for his hospitality. How can we support people who serve in ministry?
Revelation 1: John saw the risen Jesus in glory. How does that picture of Jesus affect us?
Revelation 2: The church at Ephesus had abandoned its first love. Have we lost any of our early passion for God?
Revelation 3: Jesus stands at the door and knocks. Is there an area of life where we've kept him at the door?
Revelation 4: All of heaven worships God. What does worship look like in our home?
Revelation 5: People from every nation worship the Lamb. How does that big picture change our view of the church?
Revelation 6: The martyrs cried out, 'How long?' What injustice in the world makes us cry out?
Revelation 7: God will wipe away every tear. What tears are we looking forward to having wiped away?
Revelation 8: The prayers of the saints rise like incense. How does it feel to know our prayers matter?
Revelation 9: Despite plagues, people did not repent. What does it take for people to change?
Revelation 10: John was told to eat a scroll that was sweet and then bitter. When has God's word been both sweet and hard for us?
Revelation 11: The two witnesses were faithful to the end. Who are faithful witnesses we admire?
Revelation 12: The believers overcame by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony. What is our testimony?
Revelation 13: The beast demanded worship from everyone. What pressures us to compromise?
Revelation 14: 'Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord.' How do we think about death and heaven?
Revelation 15: The redeemed sing the song of Moses and the Lamb. What song would we sing about what God has done for us?
Revelation 16: Even in judgment, God is called just. How do we balance God's love and justice?
Revelation 17: Babylon looked glamorous but was empty. What glamorous things tempt us?
Revelation 18: Merchants mourned the loss of their wealth. How tightly do we hold our possessions?
Revelation 19: The wedding supper of the Lamb is a celebration. How does our marriage reflect God's love for his people?
Revelation 20: The books were opened and everyone was judged. How does knowing that shape how we live?
Revelation 21: God will make all things new. What are we most looking forward to in the new creation?
Revelation 22: 'Come, Lord Jesus.' How do we feel about Jesus' return?
